expects.rule: One column, one field per row, label above the field. Remove any field whose data can be derived or collected later (NN/g cites a form cut from 6 fields to 2). Keep optional fields to 1 or 2 and label them as optional.

Errors use more than colour: outline the field, red text and heavier type, say what is wrong and keep what the user typed. NN/g cites 78% one-try error-free submissions for forms that follow guidelines against 42% for forms that break them (Seckler et al., CHI 2014).
Do not use placeholder text in place of a label.

In a shop, offer guest checkout as the most prominent choice, above or next to sign-in, and ask for an account at the confirmation step. Baymard reports 18% of users abandon a checkout when forced to create an account.

Do not make login depend on remembering a password or solving a puzzle without an alternative. Allow password managers, autofill and pasting, including pasting a verification code (WCAG 2.2 criterion 3.3.8, Level AA).

Information already entered in the same process is filled in or offered for selection; browser autocomplete alone does not meet it. A new hidden password may still be asked twice (WCAG 2.2 criterion 3.3.7, Level A).
Offer single sign-on with the providers the audience already uses, next to email, so the shortest path is one click.
State the password rule where the user creates the password, visible at that moment, rather than after a failed attempt or behind a link.

traits: 7 of 7 offer Google; 4 of 7 add Microsoft (Cal.com, Calendly, Auth0, Asana), 2 add GitHub (Vercel, Auth0), 2 offer SAML (Linear, Cal.com), and Vercel adds Apple and ChatGPT.
3 of 7 show an email input at once (Calendly, Auth0, Asana); 3 hide email behind a button (Linear, Vercel, Cal.com); Stripe asks four fields.
The heading is under 10 words on 7 of 7 and names the task or the free offer; 3 of 7 add 'No credit card required' (Calendly, Auth0, Asana).
4 of 7 use one centred column or modal (Linear, Stripe, Vercel, Asana); 3 of 7 split the screen with a brand or product panel (Cal.com, Calendly, Auth0).
6 of 7 show a link to the other state (Sign in, Log In, Sign up) on the first screen.
4 of 7 show a cookie banner or dialog over the first screen, covering part of the form on Calendly, Auth0 and Asana.
4 of 7 use one typeface family (Linear, Stripe, Vercel, Asana); labels sit above fields on Stripe and Asana, while Calendly uses placeholder text only.
Colour is held back: white or pale grey on 5 of 7, one accent on the main button (periwinkle, blue, dark).

avoid: A sign-up form of more than five fields before the user sees the product.
Blocking paste in the password or code field, or asking for a code that must be retyped from another screen.
Placeholder text as the only label, which disappears when the user types.
Password rules revealed only after a failed submit, or an error that says Invalid input without naming the field.
A CAPTCHA puzzle as the only way to prove the user is human, with no alternative.
A forced account before checkout or before the first useful action in the product.
Asking for the same email or address twice in one flow.
